title: Flat scalar restriction preserves K-flat complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $\varphi:R\to B$ a homomorphism of commutative ring sheaves. Use sheaf modules, sheaf tensor, total tensor of cochain complexes, K-flatness, flatness, and restriction of scalars as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], [def-pc-kflat-complex], [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Assume $B$ is flat over $R$. If $P$ is a possibly unbounded K-flat $B$-complex, then $\operatorname{Res}P$ is K-flat over $R$. If every term of $P$ is flat over $B$, every term of $\operatorname{Res}P$ is flat over $R$.

source.place: Tag 06YN (definition-K-flat) and Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), scalar-change K-flat argument; tensor balancing in sites-modules.tex, Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product).

proof.text: Write $U=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$, and let $V_R,V_B$ forget to abelian sheaves. By restriction of scalars, $V_RU=V_B$ on objects and maps. The forgetful-functor node says that both forgetful functors are faithful and preserve kernels, cokernels and all small colimits. They detect zero objects: if $V_RM=0$, faithfulness gives $1_M=0$, and likewise over $B$. Thus they detect exactness, by the kernel/image description of homology. It follows that $U$ is exact and preserves and reflects acyclicity. It also commutes with small direct sums: the underlying direct sum and its $R$-action are the same on both sides, since the action is uniquely determined by its composites with all summand inclusions. These observations use only small diagrams; the diagonals of total tensor below are indexed by subsets of $\mathbf Z^2$.

Let $E(M)=M\otimes_R B$ with its $B$-module structure. The extension/tensor comparison, and symmetry of sheaf tensor, identify $UE(M)$ with $M\otimes_R U(B)$. This identification is natural in $M$: for $f:M\to M'$ the two composites $M\otimes_R U(B)\to UE(M')$ agree after composing with the module sheafification unit of the presheaf tensor, because both send the image of a local pure tensor $m\otimes b$ to the image of $f(m)\otimes b$ under the scalar-extension unit; a map out of a module sheafification is determined by its composite with the unit. Since $B$ is flat over $R$, the latter functor is exact by the definition of flatness. Applying this to a short exact sequence, and using the exactness detection in Step 1, shows that $E:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(B)$ is exact. In particular, for any acyclic, possibly unbounded $R$-complex $A$, apply the exact-functor cohomology node degree by degree to obtain $H^i(E(A))\cong E(H^i(A))=0$ for every $i$. Hence $E(A)$ is an acyclic $B$-complex. This is exactness in sheaf modules, not exactness on sections over each object.

For an $R$-module sheaf $M$ and a $B$-module sheaf $N$, the sheaf tensor universal property gives mutually inverse $R$-linear maps $\beta_{M,N}:M\otimes_R U(N)\longrightarrow U((M\otimes_R B)\otimes_B N)$ and $\gamma_{M,N}$, specified on local pure tensors by $m\otimes n\mapsto(m\otimes1)\otimes n$ and $(m\otimes b)\otimes n\mapsto m\otimes bn$. Give $M\otimes_R U(N)$ a $B$-action as follows. The presheaf tensor $Q(V)=M(V)\otimes_{R(V)}N(V)$ is a presheaf of $B$-modules by $c(m\otimes n)=m\otimes cn$ (well defined since $c$ acts $R(V)$-linearly on $N(V)$; compatible with restrictions). By the module-sheafification interface (with the sheaf of rings $B$), its abelian sheafification, which is the underlying abelian sheaf of $M\otimes_R U(N)$, carries a unique $B$-module structure extending this action, and the unit $Q\to M\otimes_R U(N)$ is $B$-linear; restricted along $\varphi$ it is the given $R$-structure, by the uniqueness of the compatible action map for $R$. The map $\beta$ composed with this unit is sectionwise $B$-linear, so by the uniqueness of factorization through the unit $\beta$ is $B$-linear; hence so is $\beta\gamma$. For the inverse, $R$-balancing follows from $(rm)\otimes bn=m\otimes\varphi(r)bn$, and $B$-balancing from $m\otimes(bc)n=m\otimes b(cn)$. The cited bilinear extension theorem extends these sectionwise pairings through the inner sheafification; the tensor universal property then extends them through the outer tensor. The forward pairing is $R$-balanced by the same relations. Both composites are identities: one fixes $m\otimes n$, and the other sends $(m\otimes b)\otimes n$ to $(m\otimes1)\otimes bn=(m\otimes b)\otimes n$. Uniqueness in the cited universal properties proves the identities on sheaves and naturality in both $M$ and $N$. No assertion that sections of a sheaf tensor are sectionwise tensors is used.

proof.text: Apply $\beta_{A^p,P^q}$ from Step 3 on every summand $p+q=n$. The direct-sum description of total tensor and Step 1 give an isomorphism of graded $R$-module sheaves $\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_R U(P))\cong U(\operatorname{Tot}(E(A)\otimes_B P))$. It is an isomorphism of complexes: on the summand indexed by $(p,q)$, both ways around the differential square send $a\otimes x$ to $(d_Aa\otimes1)\otimes x+(-1)^p(a\otimes1)\otimes d_Px$. The differential of $E(A)$ is induced by $d_A$, and $B$ is in degree zero. Equality on local pure tensors gives equality on each sheaf tensor by the uniqueness in Step 3, and equality after all summand inclusions gives equality on the direct sum. The inverse from Step 3 commutes with the differential because it is the inverse of this chain map. Only direct sums occur, including when both complexes are unbounded.

Now take any acyclic $R$-complex $A$. Step 2 makes $E(A)$ acyclic over $B$. By the given K-flatness of $P$ and the definition of K-flatness, $\operatorname{Tot}(E(A)\otimes_B P)$ is acyclic over $B$. Exact restriction in Step 1 makes its restriction acyclic over $R$, and the chain isomorphism of Step 4 identifies that restriction with $\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_R U(P))$. Since $A$ was arbitrary, this is precisely the defining acyclic-tensor test for $U(P)$ to be K-flat over $R$.

Finally suppose every $P^q$ is flat over $B$. For a short exact sequence of $R$-module sheaves, Step 2 gives a short exact sequence after applying $E$. Tensor it over $B$ with $P^q$, which preserves exactness by the definition of flatness, and then apply the exact functor $U$ of Step 1. Naturality in $M$ of the isomorphism in Step 3 identifies the resulting sequence with the original short exact sequence tensored over $R$ with $U(P^q)$. Thus the functor $-\otimes_R U(P^q)$ is exact. By the definition of flatness, $U(P^q)$ is flat over $R$ for every $q$. This argument is separate from the K-flat test and does not assume that a K-flat complex has flat terms.
